transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-08
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Tom Reynolds (CTO - Quantum Bridge), Maya Lee (ML Eng), Jordan Park (DevOps), Eli Zhao (Product)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery for PLG/self-serve Redwood API. Customer evaluating hosted first, possible Dedicated later. Interested in quickstart, free credits, time-to-first-token, and basic security posture (SOC2, SSO, VPC). Agreed to share sample data and run a short benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Tom: Good, thanks. Tom here, CTO. We only have about 45 minutes so we'll try to get through our questions.
[00:14] Alex: Perfect. Goal for today is quick discovery — understand your stack, latency/cost constraints, and see if the PLG quickstart is a fit. We'll also cover how fast you can get to first token with our hosted API and what Dedicated/Private options look like if you need them later.
[00:29] Priya: Quick intro from me — I usually run the technical bits: SDKs, benchmarks, and what we recommend for small pilots.
[00:36] Maya: Hi, Maya. I run models and infra for our chat product. We're exploring adding a response-generation endpoint and some embeddings for search.
[00:45] Jordan: Jordan, DevOps. We'll care about network, VPC, and keys.
[00:50] Eli: Eli on product, mostly here to understand timelines and pricing.
[00:54] Alex: Great. First quick question — what's your current stack for models and serving?
[01:02] Tom: Right now we run a mix — some internal models on managed EC2/GPU, and for a few experimental features we call OpenAI. Cost is getting high and latency is a problem for multi-tenant stuff. We're evaluating alternatives.
[01:16] Maya: We're interested in better unit economics and more predictable latency, especially at 90th pct. We also want simple onboarding so product teams can iterate without ops blocking them.
[01:26] Alex: That maps well to our PLG approach. You can spin up hosted API access, use free credits, and get to first token in minutes via the SDK. If you later need Dedicated for predictable capacity or Private for VPC/on-prem, that's an upgrade path.
[01:40] Jordan: A few specific constraints — must be able to do SSO via SAML, audit logs for compliance, and encryption with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). Also, any chance of running in our VPC?
[01:51] Priya: We support SSO/SAML and have SOC 2 docs. For KMS, Redwood Private can integrate with customer KMS in Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted offers encryption-at-rest and in-transit but not customer-managed KMS unless you contract for Private. For VPC, Dedicated and Private have VPC options — Hosted is internet-facing.
[02:10] Tom: Okay, so for a first pass we want to try hosted to validate product/quality, but security will be a check before committed spend.
[02:18] Alex: Totally reasonable. The hosted quickstart gives you the API key, SDK snippet, and free credits to test throughput. Time-to-first-token for simple text generation is typically under 5 minutes from signup if you follow the quickstart. We also provide a curl example and example code for streaming.
[02:36] Maya: What's the free credits amount? And any rate limits?
[02:40] Alex: New accounts usually get $300 of credits for 30 days in the PLG quickstart. Rate limits exist by default but we can raise them if you show early usage or during a pilot.
[02:50] Jordan: When you mention raising limits, is that automated or sales?
[02:54] Alex: For moderate bumps it's self-service via the console; for larger increases we coordinate with the account team.
[02:59] Priya: On the technical side, for embeddings and chat we recommend batching for efficiency. The SDK has automatic batching and a pre-built caching layer for KV cache/prefix caching to reduce token costs. Note — sometimes our transcriptions call KV 'cash' — but it's cache, the mechanism for reusing prefixes.
[03:18] Tom: Nice. How about latency and models — we care about 50–100ms token latency for short prompts. Any baseline numbers?
[03:26] Priya: For our hosted endpoints, on modern GPU-backed instances we see average per-token latencies in the ~30–80ms range depending on model size and sequence length. We publish verified profiles in the catalog so you can pick a cost/perf sweet spot. If you need tighter SLOs we recommend Dedicated where you can reserve capacity and control autoscaling behavior.
[03:46] Maya: If we start with hosted, is model version pinning possible? We don't want a sudden model change breaking UX.
[03:52] Alex: Yes, you can pin to a model version and then follow a rollout policy. Our Console supports canary and A/B deploys and automatic fallback to a older model or a smaller variant if a problem is detected.
[04:05] Jordan: For benchmarking, what's the best way to run a realistic test — do you provide a script?
[04:09] Priya: Yes, we'll provide a benchmark checklist and a small load-test script using our SDK. We'll also run a short joint benchmark during the demo if you want.
[04:17] Tom: That'd be great. We want to compare costs vs OpenAI and Anthropic. Any rough percent improvements?
[04:24] Alex: It varies by workload. With batching, caching, and model selection you can often get 20–50% better unit cost vs generic endpoints, and Dedicated can push further. We'll include cost estimates in the pricing sheet we send.
[04:36] Eli: On onboarding friction — how long to get engineers comfortable? Any docs or example apps?
[04:41] Priya: Quickstart repo, SDKs in JS/Python, examples for embeddings and chat, and an interactive tutorial. Many teams get a simple prototype running in under a day; time-to-first-token usually under 10 minutes if keys are configured.
[04:56] Maya: Are there any limitations on data retention for hosted? We can't send PII without controls.
[05:00] Alex: Hosted has configurable retention — by default short retention for PLG accounts, and you can opt for no retention for Dedicated/Private deployments. We'll share our security overview and data handling docs.
[05:12] Jordan: For network, we need IP allowlisting and audit logs.
[05:16] Priya: IP allowlisting is supported on Dedicated; hosted supports API token restrictions and we can log requests with metadata. For full audit logs and SIEM integration, Dedicated/Private is the path.
[05:28] Tom: Sounds like the hosted trial is fine to validate model quality and dev experience. If numbers look good we'll scope a Dedicated pilot. Timeline wise, we're hoping to have a pilot in the next 4–6 weeks.
[05:39] Alex: Great. For the pilot we usually recommend starting with the PLG quickstart, then a 2-week proof-of-concept on Hosted with our free credits. If that looks promising, we scope Dedicated sizing and an SLA conversation.
[05:52] Eli: Any gotchas for streaming vs non-streaming? We're leaning streaming for UX.
[05:57] Priya: Streaming is supported in the SDK and the REST API. For low-latency UX make sure you use the streaming path to show intermediate tokens — that prevents waiting for the full generation. Also, watch your batch sizes and max tokens to avoid tail latency.
[06:15] Tom: Can we run a small test now? Maybe a token estimate and a sample prompt?
[06:20] Alex: We can walk through a quick curl example but we won't execute it on this call. I'll send a quickstart link with code snippets. The steps: sign up, verify email, get API key, run example prompt that returns in seconds.
[06:33] Jordan: About SSO and SAML — is setup manual? We need SCIM provisioning ideally.
[06:38] Priya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning on enterprise accounts. For PLG accounts you can use invite links; SSO/SCIM is part of enterprise onboarding.
[06:51] Maya: Regarding cost controls — can we set hard spend limits per team?
[06:55] Alex: Yes, the Console supports quotas and per-token billing visibility. You can set route-level quotas and alerts.
[07:04] Tom: One more question on data residency — we operate in EU and need GDPR controls. Can you guarantee region isolation?
[07:11] Priya: We have region options and can deploy Dedicated/Private into specific cloud regions for data residency. Hosted has regionized endpoints but for strict regulatory requirements we recommend Dedicated/Private with contractual terms.
[07:24] Eli: Any references or case studies for customers who started on hosted and moved to Dedicated?
[07:29] Alex: Yes, we'll share a short case study and customer names in the follow-up.
[07:34] Tom: Ok, sounds good. A couple of items we'd want in writing: free credit amount and expiry, sample benchmark script, security docs (SOC2, encryption at rest, KMS options), and a rough pricing estimate.
[07:47] Alex: We'll send all that. To recap, action items: we'll send quickstart + credits instructions, Priya will schedule a demo and prepare a benchmark checklist, and Maya will share sample data and token estimates.
[07:59] Priya: I'll follow up with calendar invites for the demo and include the benchmark plan.
[08:03] Jordan: Thanks, that works.
[08:06] Tom: Thanks both.

End of transcript.

Notes: slight transcription artifacts present (names, acronyms). References to KV cache occasionally transcribed as 'KV cash'. Links to quickstart and security docs to be included as follow-up.
